- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes or high values.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when recent history shows mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward spikes in history; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 30-day forecast, especially when history includes recent highs.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust downward quickly, often holding too high for 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes; tends to smooth out sharp declines or recoveries.
- Forecast mean reversion is too aggressive — model often overshoots and then corrects too quickly, missing intermediate dips.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, especially when history includes multiple consecutive spikes or drops.
- In low-price regimes, model tends to underestimate the true price, especially if recent history is below 70.00.
